newsitem.title: COSTA RICA: Debt payments said strangling Costa Rica finances.
newsitem.headline: Debt payments said strangling Costa Rica finances.

text.p: Payments on Costa Rica's internal and external debt are strangling the nation's finances, Finance Minister Francisco de Paula said on Monday.
The payments will reach 36.0 percent of the general budget in 1997, he said at a news conference.
The internal debt reached about $2.5 billion in June.
"The levels at which the internal public debt has reached mean that small variations in interest rates cause a large impact on public finances," he said.
The government said that its external debt was about $3.4 billionn.
De Paula also unveiled a spending plan for 1997 of about $2.5 billion, 23.7 percent more than in 1996.
The budget deficit will be about 2.7 percent of gross domestic product, and will be financed by the floating of bonds, he said.
The finance minister said that inflation could reach about 10.0 percent in 1997.
